dedupe_keys.name: bayesian nash equilibrium informed agent based model of pedestrian evacuation in tunnels and constricted spaces netlogo

description: This NetLogo model simulates pedestrians evacuating from tunnels and other constricted spaces, with a game-theoretic decision rule. It was written by Yiyu Wang, Jiaqi Ge and Alexis Comber. Two peer-reviewed releases are in the CoMSES library: the first (2022) models evacuation of a tunnel and accompanies a 2023 paper in the Journal of Artificial Societies and Social Simulation; the second (2023) extends it to different constricted spaces and accompanies a GIScience 2023 short paper. Three behaviour models can be compared: shortest route, random following and Bayesian Nash Equilibrium, in which rational agents anticipate each other's moves. Experiments follow common features of past mass trampling accidents and show herding and self-organised queuing. Both releases are free to download from CoMSES; version 2.0.0 is under GPL-3.0 and version 1.0.0 under CC-BY-SA-4.0, each with a DOI. Caveats: the spaces are idealised. Coverage is general. Simulation uses: crowd safety planning for tunnels, stations and venues, and comparing behaviour assumptions in evacuation models. Related records: the GIDAI EvacTunnel model (model-gidai-evactunnel) covers road tunnel evacuation.
inputs: Geometry of a tunnel or constricted space
Pedestrian numbers and choice of behaviour model (shortest route, random follow or BNE)
name: Bayesian Nash Equilibrium informed agent-based model of pedestrian evacuation in tunnels and constricted spaces (NetLogo)
outputs: Evacuation times and emergent patterns such as herding and queuing
